summary_text: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Valparaíso/Viña: Chile's bohemian port-university culture; criminality is general rather than gender-targeted. Regional evidence: by a wide margin the country's highest-incidence region for anti-LGBTI discrimination - in 2024 it concentrated 51.32% of all national recorded cases (Metropolitana second at 25.12%), up 80.93% over 2023. In 2025 recorded cases fell here alongside Metropolitana while all 14 other regions rose; Movilh reads this as a decentralisation of hate toward territories with less LGBTIQ visibility and debate, not a local improvement. Scored relative to the national score (0.72) for Chile.

sources.title: Chile | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for Chile (updated March 2026): same-sex marriage and adoption since March 2022; hate-crime law covering SOGI since 2012; self-determination legal gender recognition since 2019; first lesbophobic-femicide conviction in 2025 (Art. 390 ter); national pushback - a parliamentary commission approved in May 2025 portrays gender-affirming care as a threat to children and recommends banning minor hormones; the Gender Identity Support Program (PAIG) was excluded from the 2026 budget; José Antonio Kast's 2025 presidential election win flagged by civil society. National-level context.

sources.title: 2024 was ‘year of regression’ for LGBTQ rights in Chile
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (March 19, 2025): "2024 was year of regression for LGBTQ rights in Chile" - national framing: the Cass-report-inspired parliamentary commission on trans youth and the broader 2024-2025 backlash trends.

Movilh XXIV Annual Human Rights Report on sexual and gender diversity in Chile (published March 2026, covering 2025): Valparaíso concentrated 51.32% of national recorded anti-LGBTI discrimination cases in 2024, up 80.93% over 2023; in 2025 cases fell only in Valparaíso and Metropolitana while all other regions rose - Movilh reads this as the decentralisation of hate toward territories where LGBTIQ themes have less visibility; full per-region and per-commune series 2002-2025.
